name: Question 6
problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1),1-5t⟩$ at the point where $t=0,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
worked_solution:
At the point where $t=0,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(0)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(0)+u{r}^{′}(0),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({0}^{2}+1),1-5(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-5t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+1},-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨\frac{2(0)}{{0}^{2}+1},-5⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=0$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨0,1⟩+u⟨0,-5⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 6
?

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨ln⁡(t2+1),1−5t⟩ at the point where t=0, valid for all real values of u?

a
 ⟨0,1⟩+u⟨2,0⟩
b
⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨2,0⟩
c
⟨0,1⟩+u⟨2,−5⟩
d
⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨0,−5⟩
e
⟨0,1⟩+u⟨0,−5⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

At the point where t=0, the vector r′(0) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as R(u)=r(0)+ur′(0),u∈(−∞,∞)

First, we find r(0): r(0)=⟨ln⁡(02+1),1−5(0)⟩=⟨0,1⟩

Now, we calculate r′(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(ln⁡(t2+1)),ddt(1−5t)⟩=⟨2tt2+1,−5⟩

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=0: r′(0)=⟨2(0)02+1,−5⟩=⟨0,−5⟩

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where t=0 is
R(u)=⟨0,1⟩+u⟨0,−5⟩,u∈(−∞,∞).
